newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU ENDS FLAT, MARKET AWAITS C.BANK MOVES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU ENDS FLAT, MARKET AWAITS C.BANK MOVES.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Wednesday flat at 5,550/700 to the dollar after sliding in early trading from Tuesday's 5,450/600 with traders waiting for the central bank to intervene.
"Everybody holds on to dollars. Hard currency offer is pretty scarce while the money market remain flooded with leu funds," said one trader.

Some operators said the central bank (BNR) might intervene to ease pressure on the market mainly because of the presence in Bucharest of IMF chief negotiator Poul Thomsen, who arrived in Romania on Tuesday for talks on a new stand-by accord.
"The IMF people are in town so I expect the BNR to show more flexibility by trickling in some hard currency," one said.

The International Monetary Fund agreed to cancel a previous $460 million three-year standby accord, suspended last year after foreign exchange market curbs and overspending by the former leftist government.
Talks with the Fund on a new accord started on Wednesday and are expected to take up to three weeks. They coincide with ongoning loan talks with the World Bank and the European Union.
At the licensed money changing bureaux the dollar fetched some 6,200 lei but most currency shops were reluctant to sell.
Money market traders said they expected the BNR to cut the one-week funds offer at the refinancing auction on Thursday, in a move to tighten further its monetary policy.
"We had only few deals today, mainly on overnight, at prices near 49-50 percent. We hope the central bank will drain some leu liquidity from the market tomorrow," said one trader.
Last week the BNR jacked up its minimum permitted rate to 65 percent from 53 percent and offered 1.1 trillion lei, down from a previous 2.1 trillion.
